events.title: Matthew Presents Jesus' Genealogy
events.description: Matthew traces Jesus' ancestry through Abraham and David, organizing the generations around Israel's monarchy and Babylonian exile.

events.title: Joseph Receives a Dream About Jesus' Birth
events.description: When Mary is found to be pregnant, Joseph plans a quiet separation. An angel explains the child's divine conception and mission, so Joseph takes Mary as his wife and names her son Jesus.

events.title: Magi Honor Jesus at Bethlehem
events.description: Visitors from the East follow a star to Judea, consult Herod's court, and find the child with Mary at Bethlehem. They offer valuable gifts and return home by another route after a warning in a dream.

events.title: Jesus' Family Flees to Egypt
events.description: Warned in a dream that Herod intends to kill the child, Joseph takes Jesus and Mary to Egypt by night. They remain there until Herod's death.

events.title: Herod Kills the Children Around Bethlehem
events.description: Enraged that the eastern visitors did not return, Herod orders the killing of young boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity according to the timeframe he had learned.

events.title: Jesus' Family Returns and Settles in Nazareth
events.description: After Herod's death, Joseph brings the family back to Israel. Fear of Archelaus and another dream lead them away from Judea to Nazareth in Galilee.

events.title: John the Baptist Calls Judea to Repentance
events.description: John preaches in the Judean wilderness and baptizes people confessing their sins in the Jordan. He warns religious leaders to produce the fruit of repentance and announces one who will come with greater power.

events.title: John Baptizes Jesus
events.description: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John in the Jordan. As he emerges, the Spirit descends upon him and a heavenly voice identifies him as God's beloved Son.

events.title: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness
events.description: After fasting for forty days and nights, Jesus resists three temptations concerning provision, divine protection, and dominion. The devil departs and angels attend him.

events.title: Jesus Begins His Galilean Ministry
events.description: After John's arrest, Jesus moves to Capernaum and begins proclaiming repentance and the nearness of heaven's kingdom throughout Galilee.

events.title: Jesus Calls Four Fishermen
events.description: Beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus calls Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John. The four leave their fishing work to follow him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches and Heals Throughout Galilee
events.description: Jesus travels through Galilee teaching in synagogues, announcing the kingdom, and healing many illnesses. His reputation spreads beyond the region and large crowds follow him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches the Character of Kingdom Life
events.description: On a mountain Jesus teaches his disciples and the crowds about those who receive divine favor amid humility, mercy, peacemaking, persecution, and longing for righteousness. He describes his followers' public vocation through images of salt and light.

events.title: Jesus Teaches the Fulfillment of the Law
events.description: Jesus presents his mission as fulfilling the law and prophets. He applies righteousness to anger, desire, marriage, truthful speech, retaliation, and love for enemies.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Hidden Piety and Prayer
events.description: Jesus instructs his hearers to give, pray, forgive, and fast for God rather than public admiration. He gives them a pattern of prayer centered on God's holiness, kingdom, provision, forgiveness, and deliverance.

events.title: Jesus Teaches Trust Beyond Possessions and Anxiety
events.description: Jesus contrasts heavenly treasure with divided service to wealth. He directs his hearers away from anxiety over daily needs and toward trust in the Father's care and pursuit of God's kingdom.

events.title: Jesus Concludes the Sermon With a Call to Obedience
events.description: Jesus addresses judgment, prayer, treatment of others, false prophets, and the paths leading to life or destruction. He closes by comparing those who act on his teaching to a house built on rock, and the crowds recognize his authority.

events.title: Jesus Cleanses a Leper and Heals a Centurion's Servant
events.description: Jesus touches and cleanses a man with leprosy, then heals a centurion's paralyzed servant from a distance. He commends the Gentile officer's confidence in his authority.

events.title: Jesus Heals Peter's Mother-in-Law and Many Others
events.description: At Peter's house Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law, who rises and serves him. That evening he releases many from demons and diseases.

events.title: Jesus Stills a Storm and Frees Two Demoniacs
events.description: After warning would-be followers about the cost of discipleship, Jesus crosses the lake, rebukes a violent storm, and amazes his companions. On the far shore he drives demons from two men into a herd of pigs, after which the local people ask him to leave.

events.title: Jesus Forgives a Paralytic and Calls Matthew
events.description: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man despite scribal objections to his authority. He then calls Matthew from the tax booth and shares a meal with tax collectors and sinners.

events.title: Jesus Answers a Question About Fasting
events.description: Asked why his disciples do not fast like other groups, Jesus compares his presence to a wedding celebration and uses images of new cloth and wine to describe the new situation.

events.title: Jesus Restores a Girl and Heals a Suffering Woman
events.description: While Jesus goes to a leader's dead daughter, a woman suffering twelve years touches his garment and is healed. Jesus then takes the girl by the hand and raises her.

events.title: Jesus Heals Two Blind Men and a Mute Man
events.description: Two blind men appeal to Jesus and receive sight, and a demonized man is enabled to speak. The crowds marvel while Pharisees attribute the exorcisms to demonic authority.

events.title: Jesus Sends the Twelve to Israel
events.description: Moved by the distressed crowds, Jesus appoints and sends twelve disciples to proclaim the kingdom and heal. He instructs them about dependence, rejection, persecution, courage, divided loyalties, and the welcome given to his messengers.

events.title: Jesus Responds to John the Baptist's Messengers
events.description: From prison John sends disciples to ask about Jesus' identity. Jesus points to his works, then honors John's prophetic role while comparing the generation's rejection of both John's austerity and his own table fellowship.

events.title: Jesus Rebukes Unrepentant Towns and Invites the Weary
events.description: Jesus denounces towns that witnessed his deeds without repenting, gives thanks for revelation granted to the humble, and invites the burdened to learn his gentle way.

events.title: Jesus Faces Disputes Over the Sabbath
events.description: Pharisees challenge Jesus when his disciples pluck grain and when he heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath. Jesus defends mercy and his authority, then withdraws as opponents plan his destruction.

events.title: Jesus Answers Charges About His Power
events.description: After Jesus heals a demonized man, opponents claim that he works through the ruler of demons. Jesus argues that his exorcisms demonstrate God's kingdom, warns about hardened speech, and gives the sign of Jonah to those demanding a sign.

events.title: Jesus Identifies His True Family
events.description: When his mother and brothers seek him, Jesus points to his disciples and defines his family by doing the will of his heavenly Father.

events.title: Jesus Teaches the Crowds in Kingdom Parables
events.description: From a boat Jesus tells parables of soils, weeds, mustard seed, and leaven. He explains that the parables both disclose and conceal the kingdom's growth and mixed reception.

events.title: Jesus Explains the Kingdom to His Disciples
events.description: In private Jesus explains the weeds and adds parables of hidden treasure, a valuable pearl, and a net. He describes final separation and the responsibility of those instructed for the kingdom.

events.title: Nazareth Rejects Jesus
events.description: Jesus teaches in his hometown synagogue, but residents take offense because they know his family and ordinary background. Their unbelief limits the deeds he performs there.

events.title: Herod Executes John the Baptist
events.description: Matthew recounts how Herod imprisoned John for condemning his marriage and then ordered his beheading after a banquet pledge. John's disciples bury him and report the death to Jesus.

events.title: Jesus Feeds Five Thousand
events.description: Jesus withdraws to a deserted place but compassionately heals the pursuing crowds. With five loaves and two fish he feeds more than five thousand people, and the disciples collect twelve baskets of remnants.

events.title: Jesus Walks on the Sea
events.description: During a night crossing Jesus approaches the disciples' battered boat on the water. Peter briefly walks toward him before faltering, and after Jesus enters the boat the wind stops; healings follow at Gennesaret.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Defilement and Answers a Canaanite Woman
events.description: Jesus challenges traditions that neglect God's commands and teaches that defiling conduct proceeds from the heart. In the region of Tyre and Sidon, a Canaanite woman's persistent appeal leads to her daughter's healing.

events.title: Jesus Heals Crowds and Feeds Four Thousand
events.description: On a mountain near the Sea of Galilee Jesus heals many people over three days. He then feeds more than four thousand with seven loaves and a few fish.

events.title: Peter Confesses Jesus as Messiah
events.description: After refusing opponents' demand for a sign and warning the disciples about corrupting teaching, Jesus asks who they believe him to be. Peter identifies him as the Messiah and Son of God, and Jesus declares a foundational role for him.

events.title: Jesus First Predicts His Death and Resurrection
events.description: Jesus begins to tell the disciples that he must suffer, be killed, and rise. He rebukes Peter's resistance and teaches that following him entails self-denial and willingness to lose one's life.

events.title: Jesus Is Transfigured Before Three Disciples
events.description: Six days later Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a mountain, where his appearance changes and Moses and Elijah appear. A heavenly voice identifies him as the Son to whom they must listen.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Boy and Provides the Temple Tax
events.description: Jesus frees a boy whom the disciples could not heal and teaches them about inadequate faith. After again predicting his death and resurrection, he arranges payment of the temple tax without conceding that the sons are obligated.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Life in the Community
events.description: Jesus uses a child to teach humility, warns against causing others to stumble, and describes seeking the straying member. He also gives procedures for reconciliation and teaches extravagant forgiveness through a parable of an unforgiving servant.

events.title: Jesus Teaches in Judea About Marriage and Children
events.description: After entering Judea, Jesus answers a test about divorce by appealing to God's purpose in creation. He then welcomes children brought for his blessing despite the disciples' objections.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Wealth and Kingdom Reward
events.description: A wealthy man turns away after Jesus tells him to relinquish his possessions and follow. Jesus warns about wealth, promises renewal to his followers, and tells of vineyard workers who receive equal generosity despite differing hours of labor.

events.title: Jesus Predicts His Death and Redefines Greatness
events.description: On the road to Jerusalem Jesus gives a detailed prediction of his betrayal, condemnation, crucifixion, and resurrection. When the sons of Zebedee seek places of honor, he teaches that greatness among his followers is expressed through service.

events.title: Jesus Heals Two Blind Men Near Jericho
events.description: Two blind men beside the road repeatedly appeal to Jesus as David's son despite the crowd's rebuke. Jesus compassionately restores their sight, and they follow him.

events.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem
events.description: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey and colt as crowds spread garments and branches before him. The stirred city asks who he is, and the crowds identify him as the prophet from Nazareth.

events.title: Jesus Clears the Temple and Judges a Fig Tree
events.description: Jesus drives merchants from the temple, heals blind and lame people there, and defends children's acclamation. The next morning he causes a fruitless fig tree to wither and teaches the disciples about faithful prayer.

events.title: Jesus Challenges Jerusalem's Leaders Through Parables
events.description: When leaders question his authority, Jesus counters with a question about John's baptism. He tells parables of two sons, murderous tenants, and a wedding banquet that expose refusal of God's summons and warn of judgment.

events.title: Jesus Answers Tests About Tax, Resurrection, and the Law
events.description: Jesus answers attempts to trap him concerning imperial taxation and resurrection, then identifies love of God and neighbor as the law's central commands. He closes by questioning how the Messiah can be both David's descendant and lord.

events.title: Jesus Denounces Hypocritical Leadership
events.description: Jesus warns the crowds and disciples against leaders who seek status while burdening others. He pronounces woes on scribes and Pharisees for hypocrisy, neglected justice, and participation in violence against God's messengers, then laments over Jerusalem.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Temple's Fall and His Coming
events.description: On the Mount of Olives Jesus predicts the temple's destruction and describes conflict, deception, persecution, upheaval, and the coming of the Son of Man. He urges watchfulness because the timing is unknown.

events.title: Jesus Teaches Readiness and Final Judgment
events.description: Jesus tells parables of waiting attendants and entrusted wealth to stress preparedness and faithful action. He concludes with a scene in which the nations are separated according to their treatment of vulnerable people identified with him.

events.title: Leaders Plot as Jesus Is Anointed and Judas Bargains
events.description: Jesus predicts his crucifixion while chief priests and elders plan his secret arrest. At Bethany a woman anoints him in anticipation of burial, and Judas agrees to betray him for thirty silver pieces.

events.title: Jesus Shares the Last Supper With the Twelve
events.description: The disciples prepare the Passover meal, where Jesus identifies an impending betrayal. He gives bread and a cup to interpret his approaching death in relation to his body, covenant blood, and forgiveness.

events.title: Jesus Prays in Gethsemane
events.description: After predicting the disciples' desertion and Peter's denials, Jesus prays three times in deep distress while his companions repeatedly fall asleep. He submits to the Father's will and announces the betrayer's approach.

events.title: Judas Betrays Jesus and the Disciples Flee
events.description: Judas identifies Jesus with a kiss, and an armed crowd arrests him. Jesus rejects armed resistance, explains that events fulfill scripture, and is abandoned by all the disciples.

events.title: Jesus Is Condemned as Peter Denies Him
events.description: The council hears testimony against Jesus and condemns him after the high priest questions him about being Messiah and Son of God. In the courtyard Peter denies knowing Jesus three times, then leaves in bitter grief.

events.title: Judas Dies and the Priests Buy a Burial Field
events.description: The leaders hand Jesus to Pilate. Judas returns the betrayal money and hangs himself; the priests use the silver to purchase a field for burying foreigners.

events.title: Pilate Sentences Jesus to Crucifixion
events.description: Jesus remains largely silent before Pilate. Pressured by leaders and the crowd, Pilate releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over for flogging and crucifixion, after which soldiers mock him as a king.

events.title: Jesus Is Crucified and Dies
events.description: Simon of Cyrene carries Jesus' cross to Golgotha, where Jesus is crucified between two bandits and mocked. Darkness covers the land before his death; the temple curtain tears, the earth shakes, tombs open, and the guards acknowledge his divine sonship.

events.title: Jesus Is Buried and His Tomb Is Guarded
events.description: Joseph of Arimathea places Jesus' body in his new rock-cut tomb while women watch. The following day religious leaders secure the sealed tomb with Pilate's authorization and a guard.

events.title: Women Find the Empty Tomb and Meet the Risen Jesus
events.description: At dawn after the Sabbath, an earthquake accompanies an angel's opening of the tomb. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary receive news that Jesus has risen, then meet and worship him as they go to tell the disciples.

events.title: The Guards Are Bribed to Report a Theft
events.description: Some guards report the tomb's events to the chief priests. The leaders pay them to claim that the disciples stole Jesus' body while they slept and promise protection from the governor.

events.title: Jesus Commissions the Eleven in Galilee
events.description: The eleven meet the risen Jesus on a Galilean mountain, where they worship though some hesitate. Claiming universal authority, he sends them to make and baptize disciples among all nations and to teach obedience to his commands.
